title: api-config-draft-scratchpad
content:
Personal scratchpad: API + config sketch for unified inference config (hosted/dedicated/private)

Context / goal:
- Quick working draft for a 'unified request config' shape that covers: model selection, routing preferences (latency/cost/region), caching/prefix hints, batch hints, quality constraints (temperature/penalty), fallback policy hints, and observability markers.
- Target: SDK + HTTP JSON body shape that can be extended by Dedicated / Private deployments and mapped to runtime routing rules.
- Keep shape small for first pass, allow extension hooks (metadata map, flags).

High-level constraints (from product):
- Must be compatible with hosted API simple flow (minimal required fields).
- Allow clients to pin model version or request automatic fallback variants.
- Expose cost/latency tradeoff hints so platform can choose cheaper quantized variant if within quality budget.
- Keep security: no raw KMS keys in body; reference secrets via key ids only.

Rough JSON body sketch (v0):
{
  "model": "string (name or name@version)",
  "input": "string or array (text / chat structure) - keep generic body field, SDK will shape chat/messages",
  "config": {
    "mode": "generate | chat | embed | rerank",
    "response_options": {
      "max_tokens": "int",
      "temperature": "float (0-2)",
      "top_p": "float",
      "repetition_penalty": "float"
    },
    "quality_budget": "string (e.g., 'high'|'balanced'|'cheapest')",
    "routing": {
      "preference": "latency | cost | region | reliability",
      "region": "string (e.g., us-west1)",
      "allow_fallback": "bool",
      "fallback_policy": "prefer-similar | degrade-gracefully | stop"
    },
    "batching": {
      "hint": "low | medium | high",
      "max_batch_delay_ms": "int (client hint for batching)"
    },
    "caching": {
      "prefix_cache_key": "string (optional)",
      "kv_cache_hint": "true|false"
    },
    "observability": {
      "trace_id": "string (optional)",
      "client_request_id": "string"
    },
    "metadata": {"_freeform": "map<string,string> - for extensibility (no nested objects)"}
  }
}

Notes on fields:
- model: allow both 'llama-3b@v1' and 'redwood/llama-3b-quant@q4' style. SDK should normalize.
- quality_budget: platform policy maps to model variants and quantization levels. Suggested mapping: high -> full float > balanced -> int8/16 > cheapest -> q4/q2.
- routing.prefer* vs region: combine - if preference=latency, region is a soft hint. If region provided, treat as hard constraint in private deployments.
- fallback_policy: examples: prefer-similar -> choose closest architecture+quantization; degrade-gracefully -> reduce max_tokens or precision; stop -> return 429-like error.

Examples (short):
1) Low-latency consumer read: 
POST /v1/infer
Body: { model: "redwood/gptx-7b@v2", input: "summarize: ...", config: { mode: "generate", routing: { preference: "latency" }, quality_budget: "balanced", batching: { hint: "low" } } }

2) Batch embedding job with cost focus:
POST /v1/infer 
Body: { model: "embedding-small@v1", input: [...], config: { mode: "embed", routing: { preference: "cost" }, batching: { hint: "high", max_batch_delay_ms: 200 }, quality_budget: "cheapest" } }

3) Enterprise private deploy, must not cross region:
Body: { model: "redwood/secure-bert@v1", input: "...", config: { routing: { preference: "region", region: "eu-west1", allow_fallback: false }, observability: { trace_id: "..." } } }

Mapping to runtime (notes for runtime eng):
- routing.preference + quality_budget -> routing decision tree.
  - if allow_fallback=false and requested model/region not available -> return 409/412 with 'unavailable' + suggestions block.
  - quality_budget triggers selection algorithms: pick lowest-cost variant that meets a quality threshold. Need metric mapping (per-model evals).
- caching.prefix_cache_key: translates to prefix lookup for KV cache. If present, attempt fast-path: cached_tokens -> return with X-Redwood-Cache header.
- batching.hint and max_batch_delay_ms inform dynamic batching policies per route; these are hints only for hosted, strict for dedicated (tunable per customer).

Observability & billing hooks:
- Observability.trace_id should map to X-Trace in internal pipeline; client_request_id is useful for CS ticket linking.
- Billing tags: maybe include a small list metadata.billing_tags: ["feature-x", "experiment-2026-01"] (we said no nested lists inside metadata? we allowed map<string,string> - but earlier constraint 'no nested objects' is for this dataset; the API spec can include small arrays. For JSON body spec we should avoid deep nesting in metadata).

Open questions / TODOs:
- Do we want a separate top-level 'route_hints' for advanced users who want to specify explicit pool ids? e.g. route_hints: { pool_id: "dedicated-abc" } - this leaks infra details. Maybe add in 'metadata' under a reserved key 'infra.pool_id' and only honored by enterprise.
- How to express model ensembles / rollouts? For A/B we might allow 'candidate_models': ["modelA@v1","modelB@v2"] with weights -> map to rollout system. Need to ensure SDK ergonomics and server validation.
- Security: should we allow 'kms_key_id' references in metadata? yes but only as id string, platform will validate at auth layer.
- Should 'quality_budget' be numeric (0-100) to allow fine-grained control? Might be nicer: keep both: allow short labels and optional numeric override in config.

Sketch: rollout/ensemble extension (v0-ext):
config.ensemble: { candidates: [ { model: "m1@v2", weight: 0.7 }, { model: "m2@v3", weight: 0.3 } ], metric: "perplexity|human_eval|custom:" }
(we might keep as opt-in enterprise only)

CLI/SDK ergonomic notes (Jamie):
- JS SDK: keep top-level shape flattened: client.infer({ model, input, ...config }) where config fields map directly. Provide helpers for batching.hint and caching.
- Server: validate 'model' format, quality_budget & numeric overrides. Return structured error codes: model_not_found, region_unavailable, fallback_disabled.

Example error response (draft):
{ "error": { "code": "region_unavailable", "message": "Requested region eu-west1 currently has no capacity for model X", "suggestions": ["try model@v2-quant", "remove region hint to let system pick closest"] } }

Notes to self / TODO list:
- [ ] Sync with runtime team re: 'quality_budget' mapping table (per-model thresholds). -> @Alex Chen
- [ ] Decide whether metadata allows small arrays (billing tags) or force comma-delimited string.
- [ ] Add canonical examples for chat (messages array) vs single text.
- [ ] Draft SDK sample code for JS + Python (small snippets).
- [ ] Add A/B rollout/ensemble safety & metric collection requirements.

References / links:
- Confluence draft: CONFLUENCE-API-SPEC-789 (working doc)
- GH PR: GH-PR-1023 (early server validation + schema)
- Slack: #eng-runtime thread from 2025-11-05 where we discussed 'quality_budget' labels

Last thoughts: keep the base shape intentionally forgiving. Use metadata map for edge/enterprise features. Keep limited surface for public hosted API to avoid exposing infra concepts. We'll iterate after sync with Alex (routing) and Priya (DX).

End of scratchpad.

Notes-to-self (final): save this as draft; migrate trimmed spec to confluence page and add validation examples.
